text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (grounds for eviction, notices to quit, and penalties)","requirement":"A landlord may remove a residential tenant only for the causes the Act lists, and only through a court order. This part of the document covers the later listed grounds. Criminal-conviction grounds: drug offenses (n), assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, the landlord's family or employees (o), civil-court liability for theft, assault or drug activity (p), theft of property (q), and human trafficking (r). Each of these requires a 3-day Notice to Quit before suit, except human trafficking, where the text gives no notice period. Suit must be brought within two years of the juvenile delinquency finding, the conviction or the release from incarceration, whichever is later. For human trafficking the limit is two years after the violation ended. Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order, and the landlord must prove one of the listed causes: holding over after the lease term, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, willful damage, constant violation of written rules, or violation of a lease provision with a right of re-entry. Notice periods for these tenants are 3 months for at-will or year-to-year tenancies, 1 month for month-to-month tenancies, and a 3-day written Notice to Quit for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating tenants. The same rules apply when the landlord does not renew the lease. Rooming and boarding houses must follow the Act's good-cause and notice requirements, plus at least 3 working days' notice to the County Welfare Board. Public housing tenants may request a hearing after a termination notice. Penalties: a landlord who gives an owner-occupancy notice must occupy the unit for at least 6 months, and a landlord who gives a notice to board up, demolish or permanently retire the building from residential use must not use it residentially for 5 years. Reprisal against a tenant who exercises civil rights is barred separately (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-10.10).","key_value":"3-day Notice to Quit for the criminal-conviction grounds; 3-month or 1-month notice for owner-occupied 2-3 family dwellings; 6-month owner occupancy and 5-year no-residential-use periods","coverage_conditions":"Residential tenancies in New Jersey.
